outcomes: Identify the pivot and perpendicular distance to the force line before calculating torque.
content: Torque measures turning effect about a chosen pivot. Its magnitude is force times the perpendicular distance from pivot to the force line: tau = r F sin(theta). A force directed through the pivot has zero torque. To solve: mark the pivot, extend the force line, draw the perpendicular distance, then assign clockwise or anticlockwise sign. Practice: sketch equal forces at several angles and rank their torque before computing.

outcomes: Track homologous chromosomes separately from sister chromatids; count chromosomes by centromeres.
content: Mitosis separates sister chromatids and normally preserves ploidy. Meiosis has one DNA replication followed by two divisions. In meiosis I, homologous chromosomes separate: each daughter nucleus has one member of each homologous pair, still composed of sister chromatids. In meiosis II the sisters separate. Count chromosomes by centromeres, not by DNA strands. Draw each division and track a color for each homologue.

outcomes: Determine outcome type, sampling unit and dependence before choosing a test; check assumptions.
content: Choose a test from the study design, outcome and assumptions. For a quantitative outcome measured twice in the same independent units, analyze within-unit differences; a paired t test requires suitable assumptions about those differences. For independent groups with unknown and possibly unequal variances, Welch t can compare means when its assumptions fit. Categorical counts require other methods; do not choose t tests just because there are two groups. Always state the estimand, null and sampling unit.
